reason: E1 supports that semi-coherent boundaries reduce pile-ups in the BCC phase and promote work hardening, but does not directly show that pile-ups in the FCC phase cause brittleness. E2 directly demonstrates that phase-selective recrystallization achieves ~35% elongation and ~2 GPa stress, fully supporting the intervention and predicted outcome. The mechanism linking reduced FCC dislocation density to reduced pile-ups is implied but not explicitly measured in the cited evidence.
premises: Dislocation pile-ups at semi-coherent lamellar boundaries cause stress concentration and brittle failure in the untreated EHEA.
Phase-selective recrystallization of the FCC phase can reduce dislocation density and pile-ups at these boundaries.
Reducing dislocation pile-ups will enhance ductility while retaining or increasing strength.
The treatment can achieve ~35% uniform elongation and ~2 GPa true stress.
